nodes.prompt:
You are in an isolated git worktree of the repo {{ inputs.repo }}, on
this run's own branch — fresh on the first pass, and already carrying
the previous round's commits on a feedback round. Implement this task,
keeping the diff focused and touching ONLY the files this task owns:
  {{ inputs.task }}
Add or update tests. Choose a commit granularity that fits the work —
one commit per refactoring unit for refactors, per file for sweeps, per
feature slice for new code — and state your choice in the first commit
message. Commit as you go, staging only the files you changed, by
explicit path (`git add <path> ...`) — never `git add -A`, `git add .`,
or `git add -u`. End every commit message with the trailer
`Co-Authored-By: oh-my-graph <graphs@oh-my-graph.dev>` (the attribution
convention in CONTRIBUTING.md).
Your FINAL reply IS the verdict: this node ends the moment you reply, so
work you promise to do afterwards never happens. Never end on a plan to
continue — report the state that is TRUE AS YOU REPLY. When the change
is committed, START your reply with the bare word DONE — those four
characters FIRST, no markdown emphasis (`**DONE**` is WRONG), no
heading, no preamble — then a one-line summary of what you changed.
Anything you need to qualify goes AFTER the verdict, never before it:
a line of context ahead of the token fails this node even when the
work is done.
If it is not finished, do NOT write DONE: start with a bare BLOCKED and
the current state, so this lane stops instead of shipping half a task.

Review findings from the previous round follow — they are empty on the
first pass. If present, fix every blocking finding before anything
else, and note that this lane's branch already carries the previous
round's commits: amend the work, do not restart it. Items under a
`Minor:` line are not this round's to fix: leave them unless a blocking
fix rewrites the same code anyway — they reach the PR body through the
review.
{{ feedback.review }}

Continue the work — or, on a retried attempt, start from the branch's
committed state — and {{ inputs.checks }}
Run every check SYNCHRONOUSLY and wait for it to finish — never in the
background.
If you stress tests (repeated runs under the race detector, or your
stack's equivalent), DERIVE the repetition count from this budget —
never copy a fixed one:
  1. BUDGET. This node is killed at {{ self.timeout }}, and a node
     killed by its own timeout produces NO verdict at all. Spend at
     most half of that on stress, and leave the rest for the checks
     and the verdict.
  2. DERIVE. Time ONE repetition of each package first (`-count=1`),
     then pick per-package counts so the timing runs and the stress
     runs TOGETHER fit step 1 — the budget is shared across packages,
     not granted to each. A smaller
     count that finishes beats a larger one that is killed.
  3. RAISE THE PER-TEST TIMEOUT. `go test` kills a package after 10
     minutes BY DEFAULT and prints FAIL — a failure that never
     happened. Pass `-timeout` ABOVE your step-1 budget and BELOW this
     node's bound of {{ self.timeout }}
     (`go test <pkg> -race -count=<n> -timeout <duration>`).
Your FINAL reply is the verdict: never end the turn on an
interim report. If everything succeeds, your reply is exactly the four
bare characters PASS and nothing else — no markdown emphasis (`**PASS**`
is WRONG), no heading, no backticks, no preamble. Otherwise reply FAIL,
equally bare, as the very first characters, followed by the failing step.

Review this worktree's diff vs its base for style, naming, and simplicity.
{{ inputs.focus }}
The e2e verdict was: {{ artifacts.e2e | inline }}
If the diff adds or edits test doubles or concurrency tests, also verify:
every synchronization field is actually wired (no dead channels, no
wall-clock fallback arms) and no assertion is satisfiable by a record or
node simply being absent.

Your own reply from the previous review round of this diff follows — it
is empty on the first pass. If present, the diff was reworked to answer
it: first check each of those findings and re-raise only the ones still
open. Raise a NEW finding only where the rework changed the code, or
where missing it last round was a real mistake — not a nit you could
have raised then and did not. An item you rated minor last round stays
minor unless the rework changed the code it is about; a blocking item
stays blocking while it is open. If every earlier finding is closed and
nothing new meets that bar, the verdict is CLEAN, or MINOR: if only
minor items remain open.
{{ self.previous }}

Finish the review BEFORE you reply. Your FINAL reply IS the verdict: this
node's turn ends the moment you reply, so a part of the diff you promise
to look at afterwards is never looked at. Never end on "I'll continue" —
report what you have actually judged. Judge each item by whether you
would merge with it unfixed, not by how small the fix is: a defect, wrong
behaviour, or a changed behaviour with no test is blocking; naming,
wording and simplification are minor. A reply's verdict is its worst
item. START the reply with exactly one of these three bare tokens, as the
very FIRST characters, with no markdown emphasis (`**CLEAN**` is WRONG),
no heading, no preamble:
  - CLEAN — you reviewed the whole diff and found nothing worth changing.
  - MINOR: — you found something worth changing, but nothing you raise
    blocks a merge; followed by a short bulleted list, worst first.
  - FINDINGS: — at least one item you would not merge without fixing;
    followed by the blocking items as a short bulleted list, worst first,
    then any minor items under a `Minor:` line.
Anything you need to qualify goes AFTER the token, never before it: a
line of context ahead of it fails this node even when the review is
finished.

nodes.description: Approve publishing this lane's reviewed HEAD as a pull request. Read the review at {{ artifacts.review }} and the e2e verdict at {{ artifacts.e2e }}; e2e's engine verify record (the command it ran and its exit code) is in this run's state.json beside them. Rejecting ends the run unpublished.

nodes.prompt:
Do not change anything. Reply with the bare word DONE as the very first
four characters — no markdown emphasis (`**DONE**` is WRONG), no
heading, no preamble.

verify.command: ref="refs/omg-approved/$(git symbolic-ref --short HEAD)"; test "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" = "$(git rev-parse --verify -q "$ref")"

nodes.prompt:
{{ inputs.publish }}
  {{ artifacts.review | inline }}
Your grant is exactly this: Read, `Bash(git push *)`,
`Bash(gh pr create *)`, `Bash(gh pr view *)`, `Bash(git status*)`,
`Bash(git log*)` and `Edit(./.omg-pr-body.md)` — writing ONE file,
`.omg-pr-body.md` in your working directory. Any other call is denied,
not asked about. This node never commits, amends, rebases, resets or
checks out: the HEAD you publish is the one a person approved, so push
this branch's HEAD as it is (`git push -u origin HEAD`), never another
commit and never with `--force`. A body passed inline is denied even
though it starts with `gh`: a multi-line `--body '…'`, a heredoc and a
`$(…)` are all refused. So the body goes through that file, in this
order:
  1. Write the whole body to `.omg-pr-body.md` with the Write tool (if
     an earlier run left one there, Read it first, then overwrite it).
  2. Run `gh pr create --title '<one line>' --body-file .omg-pr-body.md`,
     plus any other flag asked for above (such as `--draft`).
  3. Never `git add` or commit `.omg-pr-body.md`; it is not part of the
     change. Leave it where it is once the PR is open.
Every Bash call is ONE program, run in this working directory: no `cd`,
`&&`, `;`, `|`, redirect or heredoc. A denied call means the FORM was
wrong, not the goal: re-issue it in the form above before you give up
on it.
Open it BEFORE you reply: your FINAL reply IS the verdict, so a PR you
promise to open afterwards is never opened. START your reply with the
bare token PR followed immediately by the pull request's URL
(`PR https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/123`) — those characters FIRST,
with no markdown emphasis (`**PR**` is WRONG), no heading, no preamble.
Anything you need to qualify goes AFTER the URL, never before it: a
line of context ahead of the token fails this node even when the PR
is open.

verify.command: rm -f .omg-pr-body.md; ref="refs/omg-approved/$(git symbolic-ref --short HEAD)"; pin="$(git rev-parse --verify -q "$ref")" && test "$(gh pr view --json headRefOid --jq .headRefOid)" = "$pin" && git update-ref -d "$ref"
